title: Synthesis of camphor thiazole derivatives and its bioactivity as antioxidants
author: Cahyana, Santika, et al.
materials: All glass apparatus is cleaned and oven-dried. Homogeneity of the reaction products was verified by silica gel-coated thin layer chromatography (TLC) plate. Functional groups of product structure were identified by Shimadzu IR Prestige 21 FT-IR Spectrometer in the range 4000–400 cm−1. Maximum wavelength (λ) of a compound identified by Shimadzu UV-2450 UV–vis Spectrophotometer in the range of 200–800 nm. Chromatograms and mass spectra were detected using Liquid Chromatography Mass Spectrometry (Waters Xevo G2-S Qtof, ACQUITY UPLC®HSS C18 H-Class System). Stuart™ Analog Melting Point Apparatus was used to identify the melting point of the compound.

Camphor (synthesized from D. aromatica), sodium acetate (CH3COONa) catalyze, thiosemicarbazide, ethyl-2-chloroacetoacetate, ethanol, chloroform, aquadest, n-hexane, ethyl acetate, 2,2-diphenyl-1-picrylhydrazyl (DPPH), 4-nitrophenyl α-d-glucopyranoside, α-Glucosidase Enzyme (from Bacillus stearothermophilus), phosphate buffer, and sodium carbonate (Na2CO3) solution.

steps.title: Prepare reaction for product 1
steps.instruction: Weigh 1 mmol camphor, 1 mmol ethyl‑2‑chloroacetoacetate and 1 mmol thiosemicarbazide; dissolve them in 10 mL ethanol; add 0.02 mmol sodium acetate as catalyst.

steps.title: Reflux and workup for product 1
steps.instruction: Reflux the mixture at 78 °C with constant stirring for 10 h; cool to room temperature, then let stand overnight; pour the cooled mixture into iced distilled water, stir until a precipitate forms; collect the solid by filtration.

steps.title: Recrystallize product 1
steps.instruction: Dissolve the crude solid in a minimal amount of hot ethanol, allow it to cool slowly to crystallize camphor thiazole (product 1); filter and dry the crystals.

steps.title: Characterize product 1
steps.instruction: Perform TLC using ethyl acetate :n‑hexane = 4:1 (Rf = 0.78 for product, 0.38 for thiosemicarbazide); record melting point 210–214 °C; run LC‑UV (retention time 13.43 min) and TOF‑MS (m/z [M+H]+ = 336.1751 u, theoretical 322.1745 u); calculate isolated yield 73.24 %.

steps.title: Prepare reaction for product 2
steps.instruction: Weigh 1 mmol camphor thiazole (product 1) and 1 mmol hydrazine; dissolve both in 10 mL ethanol.

steps.title: Reflux and workup for product 2
steps.instruction: Reflux the solution at 70 °C with constant stirring for 4 h; after completion, evaporate the solvent with a dry‑air stream; collect the solid residue.

steps.title: Recrystallize product 2
steps.instruction: Recrystallize the residue from the previous step with ethanol to afford camphor thiazole‑hydrazine (product 2); filter and dry the crystals.

steps.title: Characterize product 2
steps.instruction: Run TLC with ethyl acetate :n‑hexane = 3:1 (Rf = 0.44 for product 2, 0.48 for precursor); melting point 203–206 °C; LC‑UV retention time 11.91 min; TOF‑MS [M+H]+ = 322.1764 u (theoretical 322.1701 u); isolated yield 77.36 %.

steps.title: Prepare reaction for product 3
steps.instruction: Weigh 1 mmol camphor thiazole (product 1) and 1 mmol phenylhydrazine; dissolve both in 10 mL ethanol.

steps.title: Reflux and workup for product 3
steps.instruction: Reflux at 70 °C with constant stirring for 4 h; evaporate the solvent with dry air; collect the solid residue.

steps.title: Recrystallize product 3
steps.instruction: Recrystallize the residue with ethanol to obtain camphor thiazole‑phenylhydrazine (product 3); filter and dry the crystals.

steps.title: Characterize product 3
steps.instruction: TLC using ethyl acetate :n‑hexane = 1:1 (Rf = 0.88 for product 3, 0.80 for precursor); melting point 236–240 °C; LC‑UV retention time 11.98 min; TOF‑MS [M+H]+ = 400.2115 u (theoretical 400.2171 u); isolated yield 72.91 %.

steps.title: Perform DPPH antioxidant assay
steps.instruction: Prepare sample solutions at the desired concentrations (2.0 mL each); add 2 mL DPPH solution (4 mg DPPH dissolved in 100 mL ethanol); incubate in the dark for 30 min at room temperature; measure absorbance at 517 nm with a UV‑vis spectrophotometer.

steps.title: Perform α‑glucosidase antidiabetic assay
steps.instruction: In a microplate well add 50 µL 0.1 M phosphate buffer (pH 7.0), 25 µL 0.5 mM 4‑nitrophenyl‑α‑d‑glucopyranoside (in buffer), 10 µL test sample, and 25 µL α‑glucosidase (1 mg mL⁻¹ stock in buffer); incubate at 37 °C for 30 min; stop the reaction by adding 100 µL 0.2 M Na₂CO₃; read the released p‑nitrophenol at 410 nm using a microplate reader.

steps.title: Calculate inhibition and IC50
steps.instruction: Compute % inhibition for each concentration using %Inhibition = ((Abs_blank – Abs_sample)/Abs_blank) × 100; determine IC₅₀ values from the inhibition curves for antioxidant and antidiabetic assays.
